author: unknown
why: Caption explicitly identifies the Llullaillaco massif after snowfall in Chile's national park. Snow-covered cone, blue sky and barren foreground; pixel dimensions unverified.

author: F. Millour/ESO
why: Dramatic orange sunrise behind Llullaillaco, photographed from Chile's Paranal Observatory. Centred silhouette suits a near-square crop; source lists 6000 × 4000 px.

author: D. Gadotti/ESO
why: Documented Chilean-side desert landscape with Llullaillaco on the horizon. Source lists 5181 × 3310 px; an environmental alternative with a relatively distant volcano.

author: F. Millour/ESO
why: 6000 × 4000 original TIFF. Source-confirmed Llullaillaco silhouette surrounded by brilliant orange sunrise light, photographed from Chile. Strongest colour-led poster candidate; mountain detail is silhouetted.

source: NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth
author: ISS Expedition 22 crew; Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, NASA Johnson Space Center
why: 4288 × 2929 unannotated original. Detailed astronaut photograph of Llullaillaco’s summit and distinctive lava flows; useful near-square crop and clearly documented volcano identity.

author: ESO, Dimitri Gadotti
why: 5180 × 1061 original TIFF, explicitly identified as Llullaillaco photographed from Paranal in Chile. Volcano-focused distant view; extreme panoramic proportions limit a 9:10 crop.

author: ESO/G. Lombardi (glphoto.it)
why: 5184 × 3456 original TIFF. Clear Chile-side view with recognisable snow-capped Llullaillaco; an auxiliary telescope occupies the foreground, making this a contextual alternative.

author: ESO/G.Hüdepohl (atacamaphoto.com)
why: 3419 × 4978 portrait original TIFF. Blue sky, rust-coloured desert and snow-capped Llullaillaco, explicitly identified by ESO. Observatory dominates the foreground; weaker volcano prominence but ample vertical framing.
